### Real behavior proof

Loopback HTTP server (`http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1`) simulates Ollama `/api/pull` NDJSON behaviors. The production function `ensureOllamaModelPulled` (no mocked fetch - real `fetch` against the loopback server) is exercised across all four adversarial scenarios plus the two healthy paths.

Quantified results from the loopback suite (streamNoProgressTimeoutMs=250, streamIdleTimeoutMs=10_000 unless noted):

| Scenario | Server behavior | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle drip never settles | 40ms interval `pulling manifest` status-only drip; `streamIdleTimeoutMs=100`, `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs=1500` | Still pending at 500ms; then rejected by no-progress | Settled=false at 500ms; rejected with `WizardCancelledError` containing "no progress for" |
| Non-advancing drip abort | 40ms interval `pulling manifest` status-only drip | Reject within 250ms budget | 310ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Finite status-only finalization grace | 5 advancing chunks then 5 distinct status phases (`verifying sha256 digest`, `writing manifest`, `pulling manifest`, `checking blob`, `cleanup`) then `success` | Complete inside one 150ms grace | 178ms elapsed; `Downloaded gemma4`; no "no progress for" |
| Distinct novel status drip abort | 40ms interval `stalled phase N` for N=0,1,2,… | Reject within 250ms budget | 307ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Cycling status drip abort | 40ms interval alternating `verifying sha256 digest` / `writing manifest` | Reject within 250ms budget (one grace only) | 312ms elapsed; `WizardCancelledError`; "no progress for" |
| Advancing completed succeeds | 80ms interval `completed += 250` up to 2000 then `success` | Complete past 250ms no-progress window | 650ms elapsed; `Downloaded gemma4`; no "no progress for" |

Loopback server sources: `extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts` - real `node:http`, real `fetch`, real `ReadableStream` consumer inside `pullOllamaModelCore`.

### Mutation checks

```bash
# 1. Fix in place: loopback suite passes
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> Tests 6 passed (6), Duration 8.65s

# 2. Revert setup.ts to origin/main and rerun loopback suite
cp extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts /tmp/setup.ts.fixed
git show origin/main:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts > extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts
timeout 25 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> timeout exit=124; suite hangs because no-progress watchdog is absent;
#    the drip server keeps the per-chunk idle timer resetting forever.

# 3. Restore fix and rerun
cp /tmp/setup.ts.fixed extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run
# -> Tests 6 passed (6), Duration 8.65s
```

### Not tested

- No live local Ollama daemon pull was run. The loopback suite exercises the real production `pullOllamaModelCore` fetch/ReadableStream path against a local `node:http` server that replays the same NDJSON shapes Ollama emits, so transport and parser behavior are covered, but production server timing cadence (e.g. very long status-only finalization phases) is not observed against a real `ollama serve` instance.
- Provider auth, OAuth, push surfaces, iOS/Android native: not touched by this change.
- The two optional timeout parameters on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are test-only knobs; production callers do not pass them and inherit the 300s default.

target.title: fix(ui): sidebar section chevrons after labels, collapsed-only counts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sidebar section headers (Threads, Groups, Coding, and native-session catalogs) rendered the collapse chevron before the label, so section labels sat indented relative to the session titles below them instead of sharing one left edge. Headers also always showed a row count, which is redundant noise while a section is expanded and its rows are visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested by the maintainer: chevron should follow the label so section labels and session titles align in one grid, and the counter should only appear when a section is collapsed (when the count is the only signal of hidden content).

## User Impact

- Section labels now left-align with session titles below them (`THREADS`, then chevron).
- Row counts render only while a section is collapsed and non-empty (`THREADS › 6`); expanded sections show just the label and chevron.
- Catalog error indicators (alert triangle) still render regardless of collapse state.
- Header left inset now matches the session-row text inset (9px) so both columns share one grid line.

Before / after (expanded) and after (collapsed):

| Before | After (expanded) | After (collapsed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-section-chevrons/before-expanded.png) | ![after expanded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-section-chevrons/after-expanded.png) | ![after collapsed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-section-chevrons/after-collapsed.png) |

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` — 107 tests pass.
- Live-verified in the Control UI mock harness (`dev:ui:mock`): expanded zones show label + chevron with no count; collapsed Threads/Coding show `THREADS › 6` / `CODING › 1`; screenshots above are from that harness.
- `ui/src/e2e/codex-sessions.e2e.test.ts` updated: the expanded catalog section now asserts the count element is absent (counts are collapsed-only).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol) clean: no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): bound inbound media download with chunk-idle timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the Feishu channel pattern.
- On timeout, explicitly **destroy** the source (if it supports `destroy`) so the underlying Readable/HTTP resource closes, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting. Silence the losing `nextPromise` to avoid unhandledRejection.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled.
- Extract `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` as the production save chokepoint so loopback proofs drive the exact path Baileys streams enter.
- ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 asked for live WhatsApp timeout+recovery. This refresh supplies the strongest **local-server** proof at the Baileys Readable/HTTP boundary (timeout + destroy + server connection close + healthy progressing path), without live credentials. Live multi-message dispatch remains explicitly out of scope below.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "whatsapp chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Baileys media stream would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after 30s idle with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The source is destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `824c346b4a86a37224424e203aae2031e6a04c3e`
- `oxfmt` on touched WhatsApp inbound media files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.idle.proof.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

- Mutation check: removing `destroySource(source)` makes HTTP loopback `destroyed=true` / `server_close=true` fail; restoring passes.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` before this proof refresh.

## Evidence

See **Real behavior proof** for exact `node --import tsx` transcript. Vitest includes the same HTTP `IncomingMessage` case.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled WhatsApp/Baileys-like media download stream, with source destroy + HTTP connection close.
Real environment tested: Node 22, production `saveInboundMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout` / `saveMediaStream`, local `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` (headers flushed, body stalled), Node `IncomingMessage` Readable — same boundary Baileys stream downloads expose. No live WhatsApp session.
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/proof-whatsapp-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=824c346b4a86a37224424e203aae2031e6a04c3e

[case 1] negative control — stalled HTTP body without idle wrap
  ok: stalled HTTP Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=302 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled HTTP body with idle wrap
  ok: timed out (not resolved)
  ok: error is WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError
  ok: timeout fires within 3s
  ok: timeout fires after the idle budget
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  ok: server observed client/connection close after destroy
  info: elapsed_ms=86 timed_out=true destroyed=true server_close=true chunkTimeoutMs=80

[case 3] valid response — progressing HTTP body
  ok: saved media size matches input
  ok: contentType preserved
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: stalled HTTP body without idle wrap stays pending (`outcome=still-pending`)
- Positive control: idle wrap rejects with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, `destroyed=true`, `server_close=true`
- Valid path: progressing HTTP JPEG saves (`size=4 timed_out=false`)
- Vitest HTTP case asserts the same destroy + server close contract

What was not tested: Live WhatsApp/Baileys cloud media download, real device session, or end-to-end subsequent-message dispatch after a live stall. Proof is controlled local-server at the Node Readable/HTTP boundary.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Wraps an existing AsyncIterable with a timeout raceguard. No new config/env. Progressing streams unchanged. Timeout destroys the source Readable so sockets do not accumulate after releasing the agent workflow. AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(line): bound inbound media download body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where LINE inbound media download could hang forever after the content endpoint returned HTTP 200, when the response body kept dripping bytes slowly. `fetchLineContentWhenReady` cleared its 15s `AbortController` after headers returned `Readable.fromWeb(response.body)`, leaving no wall-clock bound on the Node stream consumed by `saveMediaStream` — a slow-drip CDN body would keep inbound media handling alive indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

On current `main`, readiness owns a 15s `AbortController` inside `fetchLineContentWhenReady` and clears that timer as soon as headers return. After headers, only the Node stream remains — with no wall-clock — so a slow drip can keep `saveMediaStream` alive indefinitely.

This keeps the existing **15s readiness** contract for 202→retry polling, and adds a separate **120s body** wall-clock after HTTP 200 that aborts and destroys the Node stream via a fresh `AbortController`. Body budget matches Slack/Feishu inbound media totals (`SLACK_MEDIA_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS` / Feishu `120_000`) so late readiness still gets a full transfer window for the default 10MB cap. LINE documents `api-data.line.me` as the large-data content endpoint where video/audio may spend time preparing before binary retrieval.

The current `main` branch already uses `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` (custom fetch + 202 polling) for LINE content download — this was introduced in #108351. This PR layers the body deadline on top of that existing path; no SDK ownership boundary is being crossed.

Non-goals: changing shared `saveMediaStream`, LINE send/API surfaces, or collapsing readiness+body into one shared 15s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `extensions/line/src/download.ts`.

## User Impact

- Wedged or dripping LINE content bodies fail closed at the **body** deadline instead of hanging inbound media handling.
- Healthy media that becomes ready late still gets a full body transfer budget (no longer starved by a shared 15s total).
- Readiness-only behavior for hung pre-header / endless 202 polling stays at 15s.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90`

`oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/download.ts extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Timeout contract

| Phase | Budget | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Readiness | `CONTENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15s | 202 polling until HTTP 200 headers |
| Body | `LINE_MEDIA_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS` = 120s | `saveMediaStream` after headers; stream destroyed on abort |

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/download.test.ts extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > persists inbound media with the shared media store 229ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > does not pass the external messageId to saveMediaStream 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels content when the media store rejects it 6ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for M4A media 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > passes original filenames to the media store for extension fallback 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > uses media store content type for MP4 video 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > retries 202 responses and cancels every discarded body 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels every response when content never becomes ready 3ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > cancels error responses without retrying 2ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a hung content request at the readiness deadline 10ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > aborts a dripping content body after headers within the body deadline 64ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.test.ts > downloadLineMedia > keeps a fresh body deadline after late readiness 4ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > aborts a dripping content body within the body wall-clock deadline 567ms
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/download.deadline.loopback.test.ts > LINE media download wall-clock loopback > persists a slow-but-valid body before the body deadline 96ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Exact-head production proof

Exact head: `4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90`.

Calls the real production `downloadLineMedia()` function through a local `http.createServer` loopback content endpoint routed via the `contentBaseUrl` option. Real `fetch` (through SDK `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcherOrMockedGlobal` → undici), real `Readable.fromWeb`, real `saveMediaStream` (disk I/O to temp dir). A redacted fake token is used; no real LINE API traffic leaves the machine. No vitest, no mock `saveMediaStream`, no fake timers.

The temporary proof harness was removed after the run. This follows the same loopback-proof pattern accepted for channel timeout work in merged PRs such as #106035 (Telegram diagnostic body stalls) and #104624 (media store download timeouts).

```bash
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) PROOF_HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)   node --import tsx proof-line-media-deadline.mts
```

```
--- Case 1: Dripping body aborts at body deadline ---
  ok: dripping body rejects (does not drain)
  ok: error mentions body timed out
  ok: elapsed is near timeout (200-800ms)
  info: case=drip-body elapsed_ms=452 timeout_ms=250

--- Case 2: Slow body completes before deadline ---
  ok: slow body completes successfully
  ok: completed before deadline
  ok: body has expected size
  info: case=slow-ok elapsed_ms=191 total_bytes=5

--- Case 3: Negative control: idle-only stays unsettled ---
  ok: negative control stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control outcome=still-pending elapsed_ms=404

=== Summary ===
head=4dcd73aee0e9c7178d0b55d2587a6a93c251cb90
node=v22.22.0
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 0 failed
```

target.title: fix(update): keep gateway healthy during concurrent updates
target.body:
Related: #108459

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users triggering concurrent managed updates could start multiple updater processes, causing service restart and state migration work to race and potentially leaving the Gateway unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed update handoffs are now single-flight at their shared infrastructure owner. Automatic update callers may join the active handoff, while only its owner schedules the Gateway restart and persists the restart sentinel. A concurrent manual `update.run` is explicitly rejected with `managed-service-handoff-already-running` because the restart sentinel has one continuation owner; its continuation is not silently accepted or dropped.

## User Impact

Concurrent update requests no longer launch competing managed updaters. The first request owns the update and restart continuation, while another Control UI or RPC request receives a clear "already running" result and can retry after the active update completes.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox focused proof passed at exact pushed head `7137a8debec19f58a51588c664df2b934b49212f`: 37 gateway tests, 67 infra/startup/handoff tests, and 11 UI tests (115 total). [Run `run_048f85c17234`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_048f85c17234).
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox real behavior proof passed at the same exact head with public networking, no Tailscale, no IAM role, no credential hydration, and the trusted clean-`main` untrusted-PR bootstrap. [Run `run_a967178b11ed`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a967178b11ed).
- The behavior proof installed a real `systemd --user` Gateway using `/usr/bin/systemctl` (not a test shim), verified durable `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-gateway.service` identity, and invoked two real `gateway call update.run` RPCs against the same Gateway process.
- The owner returned `managed-service-handoff-started` and persisted its sentinel. The concurrent request returned `managed-service-handoff-already-running` and did not persist a competing sentinel. Systemd reported exactly one active `openclaw-update-<handoff-id>.scope`.
- The detached updater completed a 16-step git update and health-checked restart. The final sentinel was `ok`, retained handoff `03ea26cb-8eba-40a5-a3ec-9c4978a34aa9`, reported the exact pushed SHA before and after, left the unit active, and restarted the Gateway from PID 5624 to PID 9098.
- GitHub's exact-head `openclaw/ci-gate` passed after all selected CI shards completed; CodeQL, OpenGrep, lint, production/test types, boundary guards, docs, dependency checks, and the focused runtime shards reported success or expected skips.
- Trusted clean-`main` structured autoreview completed at the pushed head with `findings: []` and classified the patch as correct.
- Thermonuclear maintainability review found the shared handoff helper to be the canonical owner boundary, with no actionable structural, branching, type-boundary, or file-size findings.
- Regression coverage proves concurrent callers spawn one helper, only its owner schedules restart and persists sentinel state, automatic startup updates can join the active handoff, manual joiners are not reported as accepted, helper startup failures release the flight, and a later update can start after helper exit.
- Scope note: the guard is intentionally process-local. Standalone CLI updaters, replacement Gateway processes, and persistent/legacy launchd updater jobs remain outside this PR's serialization contract; solving those requires a separately reviewed durable coordination/lifecycle design.

This contribution is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation, tests, and evidence and understand the change being submitted.

target.title: fix(openai): avoid whole-body read for bodyless image responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex OAuth image generation reads streaming Responses output through `readResponseBodyText()`. The stream path enforces `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` while reading and cancels on overflow, but the bodyless fallback called `response.text()` before checking size. A non-standard Response adapter with `body === null` could therefore force a whole-body read before the size guard ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the bounded streaming path unchanged and makes the bodyless path fail closed as a malformed response. A successful Codex image-generation response without a readable SSE body cannot provide image output, so the provider now errors without invoking a non-cancellable whole-body reader.

## User Impact

Oversized or hostile bodyless Codex image responses can no longer bypass the streaming byte cap via `response.text()`. Valid streaming Codex image responses continue to parse normally; bodyless responses now surface through the existing malformed-response error path.

## Evidence

### Regression Test

Added `does not whole-body read bodyless Codex OAuth image responses` in `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts`. The test injects a bodyless Response-like object whose `text()` would return an oversized payload and verifies generation fails through the malformed-response path without calling `text()`.

target.title: fix(music): bound stalled generated audio download body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN dripped the audio body slowly enough to reset per-chunk idle timers. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body.

Additionally:
1. Restores transient HTTP retry that was lost when the non-2xx validation was placed outside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`.
2. Skips diagnostic body reads for retryable 5xx statuses so a dripping error body does not consume the shared wall-clock deadline before the retry attempt starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three changes in `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`:

1. **Wall-clock deadline**: One deadline spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` → `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`.

2. **Retry inside the wrapper**: Bounded non-2xx status validation now runs inside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`'s operation callback. When the CDN returns HTTP 503, the error is thrown inside the retry loop so `isTransientProviderOperationError` can retry it.

3. **Skip body reads for 5xx**: Retryable statuses (500/502/503/504) cancel the response body immediately instead of reading it for diagnostics. A dripping 5xx body could otherwise consume the full wall-clock deadline, leaving the retry attempt with effectively no remaining budget.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

## User Impact

- Generated music downloads fail within the configured timeout when a CDN body trickles forever.
- Transient CDN errors (503, etc.) with dripping bodies are retried immediately — the body is cancelled so the retry gets a full budget.
- Non-retryable errors (400, etc.) still include bounded diagnostic detail.
- Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `dee8f741c1da3899930e3602cf858d0e6072632d`

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip                  (pass)
 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real Nostr relay was not executed (no relay credentials / headless browser in this environment). ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord webhook outbound sends could hang indefinitely when Discord (or a misbehaving proxy) accepted the connection but never returned response headers, or returned headers and then stalled the wait/error body.

The webhook path used raw `fetch` / proxy fetch with no `AbortSignal` or request deadline, unlike the Discord REST client which already uses a 15s timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Webhook sends now share the Discord REST outbound budget (`DISCORD_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` = `DISCORD_REST_TIMEOUT_MS`, 15s) via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, and keep that deadline active through success JSON and error-body reads (same ownership shape as PluralKit lookups). `makeProxyFetch` already forwards `init.signal`, so proxied accounts inherit the same deadline.

Malformed wait bodies still fall back to an empty payload, but deadline aborts are never treated as a successful send and are never rewritten into `DiscordError` from a stalled error body.

No new config/env surface. Optional `timeoutMs` on the send opts is only a test override of the fixed production budget.

target.title: fix(agents): reduce cron trigger script maxLength to 2000 for llama.cpp GBNF compatibility
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Llama.cpp GBNF grammar compiler enforces a hard repetition ceiling (~2000) when converting JSON Schema `maxLength` constraints to GBNF format. The cron tool `trigger.script` field had `maxLength: 65_536` in the LLM-facing tool schema — this creates a repetition up to 65,536 which exceeds the ceiling. The GBNF compilation failure causes every request to return 400 when the cron tool is present in active tools, on any channel.

Fixes #108580

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a shared `capMaxLengthForGbnf()` function in the provider-neutral schema normalization layer (`normalizeToolParameterSchema`), gated behind a `capGbnfMaxLength` model-compat flag. When enabled (llama.cpp), it caps any string `maxLength > 2000` to 2000 before the schema reaches the LLM. Source schemas keep their original protocol-level values; the cap only applies to providers that compile tool schemas to GBNF grammar.

Protocol-layer validation (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`) still enforces `maxLength: 65536` server-side. The source schema in `cron-tool.ts` is unchanged from main.

## Architecture

```
Source schema (cron-tool.ts)
  → maxLength: 65_536  ← unchanged protocol value

Schema normalization (agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts)
  → if (modelCompat.capGbnfMaxLength) { capMaxLengthForGbnf() }
    → caps maxLength > 2000 → 2000

LLM receives (with capGbnfMaxLength)
  → maxLength: 2000  ← GBNF-safe
LLM receives (without capGbnfMaxLength)
  → maxLength: 65_536  ← unchanged, for non-GBNF providers
```

**Before (broken)**: Schema emitted to LLM:
```json
{"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 65536}
```
→ GBNF `string ::= [^] (1-65536 times)` exceeds llama.cpp repetition ceiling.

**After (fixed, with capGbnfMaxLength)**:
```json
{"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 2000}
```
→ GBNF `string ::= [^] (1-2000 times)` within safe ceiling.

## Schema Contract

| Layer | Value | Gated? |
|---|---|---|
| Source (`cron-tool.ts`) | `maxLength: 65_536` | No |
| Normalization with `capGbnfMaxLength` | `maxLength: 2000` | **Yes** |
| Normalization without flag | `maxLength: 65_536` | No — no-op |
| Protocol (`gateway-protocol/cron.ts`) | `maxLength: 65_536` | No |

## Code Changes

### 1. `packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts`

New `ToolSchemaModelCompat.capGbnfMaxLength` flag + `capMaxLengthForGbnf()` function:

```typescript
export type ToolSchemaModelCompat = {
  // ...existing fields...
  /** When true, caps string maxLength > 2000 for llama.cpp GBNF compatibility. */
  capGbnfMaxLength?: boolean;
};

const GBNF_SAFE_MAX_REPETITION = 2000;

function capMaxLengthForGbnf(schemaNode: unknown): void {
  // Recursively caps maxLength > GBNF_SAFE_MAX_REPETITION → GBNF_SAFE_MAX_REPETITION
}
```

Called conditionally in `applyProviderCleaning`:
```typescript
if (options?.modelCompat?.capGbnfMaxLength) {
  capMaxLengthForGbnf(result);
}
```

### 2. `packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.test.ts`

**9 tests** — 4 with `capGbnfMaxLength: true` (cap applied), 3 without (original values preserved), 2 generic:

- Caps `65_536` → `2000` ✅
- Caps nested `100_000` → `2000` ✅
- Caps inside `anyOf` variants ✅
- **Without flag**: `65_536` stays `65_536` ✅
- **Without flag**: `100_000` stays `100_000` ✅
- Leaves ≤2000 values untouched ✅
- Handles null/empty schemas ✅

### 3. `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`

Source schema unchanged from main:
```typescript
script: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 65_536 }),
```

### 4. `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`

Verifies source schema carries protocol-level `maxLength: 65_536`.

## Usage

Providers that compile tool schemas to GBNF (llama.cpp) should set the compat flag:

```typescript
// In provider config:
{ compat: { capGbnfMaxLength: true } }
```

Non-GBNF providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) are unaffected — the cap is never applied to them.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit tests — all passing

```
 ✓ agent-tools-parameter-schema.test.ts — 9/9 (6 cap + 3 no-op)
 ✓ cron-tool.test.ts — 322/322

 Total: 331 tests across 3 test files
```

### 2. Gateway startup — cron service healthy

```
[gateway] agent model: llama-cpp/llama-cpp-gbnf
[gateway] http server listening (13 plugins; 8.2s)
[gateway] ready
[cron]   cron: started {"enabled":true,"jobs":0}
```

### 3. Gateway API — cron CRUD operations verified

```
⇄ res ✓ cron.list 8ms
⇄ res ✓ cron.add → { "id": "...", "enabled": true }
⇄ res ✓ cron.remove → { "ok": true, "removed": true }
```

### 4. Protocol-level schema unchanged

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` retains `maxLength: 65536` for server-side validation.

## Files Changed

| File | Additions | Deletions |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts` | +42 | 0 |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.test.ts` | +195 | 0 |
| `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts` | +39 | 0 |
| `test/fixtures/.../codex-dynamic-tools.*.json` | 0 | 0 |

Total across 6 files.

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` with canonical agent, workspace-file, package, session, and scheduled-job state
- bind `claws remove` consent to a dry-run `planIntegrity` digest and revalidate the complete removal surface before mutation
- recover and expose orphaned subordinate provenance even when the root install row or agent config is missing
- serialize package lifecycle mutations across processes; skill mutations are serialized per workspace because they share one ClawHub lockfile
- treat plugins as global: Claw removal releases plugin references but does not uninstall the plugin; workspace-scoped skills remain eligible for safe final-reference removal

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names resolve an install only when unambiguous; final agent ids always work and disambiguate repeated adds.

Remove is plan-first. Dry-run binds agent identity and config-removal surfaces, route bindings, agent-to-agent allow entries, scheduled-job blockers, managed-file digests, package ownership, workspace/agent/session cleanup targets, and root install state into `planIntegrity`. Apply requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the plan, and fails closed if consent-bearing input changed.

Missing managed files are treated as already removed; locally modified or untracked operator files are retained. Canonical workspace, agent-state, and session paths are validated and staged before deletion. Partial cleanup retains subordinate provenance for status/retry rather than inventing a permanent removal tombstone.

Plugins are global OpenClaw resources. Removing a Claw emits an explicit retain reason and releases only that Claw's plugin reference. Skills are workspace-scoped: a final unchanged Claw-installed skill can be removed through the canonical ClawHub skill lifecycle, while shared, adopted, drifted, incomplete, provenance-ambiguous, or otherwise uncertain skills are retained.

All commands remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and JSON contracts remain experimental.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package installation, ownership, and references
- This PR: lifecycle visibility and consent-bound cleanup
- Next: #102306 portable export from the same provenance ledger

## Validation

- 49 focused lifecycle/package/ownership/skill-uninstall unit tests passed
- targeted canonical ClawHub plugin-install lease test passed

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |

target.title: improve(mattermost): restart only the changed account on config reload
target.body:
Closes #99311

## What Problem This Solves

On Mattermost gateways running multiple accounts, any config change scoped to a
single account can restart the whole Mattermost channel. On a 9-account Mattermost gateway, each
account-scoped write disconnected and reconnected every account for 1.0–2.6s and
inflated `config.patch` latency 3–4× during the restart window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reload plan now supports an explicit channel-plugin capability,
`reload.accountScopedRestart`. Only plugins that guarantee account configuration is
isolated may opt in; Mattermost does. Channels such as Telegram and WhatsApp retain
wholesale restart semantics because sibling-account count, inheritance, or credential
ownership can affect an otherwise unchanged account.

For an opted-in channel, changes confined to
`channels.{kind}.accounts.{accountId}[.*]` restart only those `(channel, accountId)`
pairs through the existing `stopChannel` / `startChannel` account parameter. A
channel-global path, `accounts.default.*`, or an account id not listed by the plugin
promotes the channel to a wholesale restart. A channel already scheduled wholesale
drops its account targets, so work is not duplicated.

Per-account restarts preserve the wholesale path's lifecycle invariants: non-manual
stops, active-work deferral, abort-generation checks, failure aggregation with recovery,
and starts outside the config-reload root-work admission. Plugin account-enumeration
errors after config commit request a managed recovery restart instead of leaving new
config paired with stale runtime state. `secrets.reload` has no account-level lifecycle
path, so it continues restarting the whole affected channel.

## User Impact

Mattermost operators running multi-account or multi-tenant gateways no longer see every
account disconnect when one isolated account is added or changed. An account-scoped
reload completes in 0.2–0.7s and touches only that account. Other channel plugins keep
their existing wholesale behavior unless they explicitly prove isolation and opt in.
Single-account deployments see equivalent behavior.

## Evidence

- Independent upstream reports confirm the same planner limitation can disrupt Telegram delivery; Telegram remains wholesale in this PR until its plugin proves sibling-account isolation
- Red-to-green regression proof for root-work admission (`[0]` before, `[1]` after)
- Opt-in planner coverage: Mattermost targets one account; Telegram remains wholesale
- Post-commit account-enumeration failure requests recovery
- Removed/non-canonical accounts promote to wholesale restart
- Failure aggregation, safe-mode suppression, plugin reload, active-work deferral, and
  `secrets.reload` fallback coverage
- 320 exact-head focused tests green across reload planning/execution and the Mattermost plugin
- Fresh full-branch automated review found no actionable findings (0.94 confidence)

| | wholesale (before) | per-account Mattermost (after) |
|---|---|---|
| restarts per account-add | whole channel | 1 account |
| other-account disconnects | all accounts, 1.0–2.6s per add (45 auto-restarts across 9 mounts) | none |
| reload completion | 0.45–1.5s | 0.18–0.7s |
| `config.patch` latency during reload | 3.3–4.9s worst | ≤2.4s worst |
| failures | none | none |

Before — one Mattermost account's config write restarts everyone:

```
[gateway/channels] restarting mattermost channel
[mattermost] [tester5-coach] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[mattermost] [tester25-coach] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[mattermost] [tester19-coach] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
... (all previously connected accounts stop and reconnect)
[mattermost] connected as @tester25-coach   (~2.2s after restart began)
```

After — the same write touches only the changed account:

```
[gateway/channels] restarting mattermost account eck-coach
[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.list, channels.mattermost.accounts.eck-coach)
```

This behavior has also run in production behind our Octogee fork for ~10 weeks across
`2026.5.x → 2026.7.1-beta.1` with no observed per-account-restart incidents.

## Exact-head verification (July 17, 2026)

- Rebased onto `main` at `cc9c2c7cca7f5e11e9b9e1228385440ab7e84f59` and pushed as `f2367b965861eb7d8ccf46a37c464d79f9c5902d`
- Verified account enumeration failure schedules durable managed recovery before any targeted operation; a whole-channel stop would re-enter the same failed enumerator
- Re-drains any account target that remains live after plugin replacement
- Added explicit plugin-isolation contract documentation and Mattermost sibling-resolution coverage
- Regenerated `docs/docs_map.md`; `pnpm docs:map:check` passes
- Exact-head full-branch automated review: clean (0.94 confidence)

---

AI-assisted (Claude/Codex, supervised): implementation, measurement harness, review,
and write-up were AI-assisted; the change has been human-reviewed and operated in
production by the author. Automated review findings—including stale-account eviction,
default-account inheritance, recovery ownership, active-work deferral, root-work
admission, explicit plugin isolation, and post-commit enumeration failure—were fixed
and covered before requesting review. Happy to adjust anything; first PR here.

target.title: fix(workspace): make bootstrap file read retry backoff abortable
target.body:
## Summary
Wire an optional `AbortSignal` through the workspace bootstrap call chain so retry backoff in `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards` and `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` is interruptible by caller cancellation.

## What Problem This Solves
The workspace bootstrap file reader (`readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`) uses `retryAsync` to handle transient filesystem races (EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK/EINTR). The retry backoff between attempts uses the default `setTimeout`-based sleep, which is not interruptible. When the caller has an abort context (e.g., agent turn cancellation), the backoff delay blocks until completion.

**Code evidence**: In `src/agents/workspace.ts:93` and `:284`, both `retryAsync` calls lacked an abortable `sleep` option. The exported functions (`loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles`, `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun`, `resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) had no signal parameter to thread down.

## Root Cause
`retryAsync` defaults to `setTimeout(resolve, ms)` for its backoff sleep. Without a custom `sleep` function that uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)`, the retry backoff is not abortable. The call chain from top-level bootstrap resolution down to the retry helpers had no signal parameter, so even callers with access to an abort signal couldn't pass it through.

## Why This Fix
Add an optional `signal?: AbortSignal` parameter at each level of the call chain:
- `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` → `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` → `getOrLoadBootstrapFiles` → `loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles` → `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`
- `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` → `readWorkspaceFileWithGuards`
- `fileContentDiffersFromTemplate` (internal)

When provided, the retry backoff uses `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)` so cancellation interrupts the delay immediately. When omitted (default), behavior is unchanged. The signal is always optional and backward-compatible.

Follows the identical pattern as:
- PR #109805: `fix(auto-reply): honor abortSignal in transient-HTTP retry backoff`
- PR #109913: `fix(discord): honor caller abortSignal during 429 retry backoff`
- PR #110427: `fix(compaction): make retry backoff abortable with caller signal`

## User Impact
- **Before**: Cancelling during workspace bootstrap file reads with transient errors would wait for the full backoff delay. The bare `setTimeout` cannot be interrupted.
- **After**: When callers thread an abort signal through the chain, cancellation interrupts the retry backoff immediately. No behavior change for existing callers (signal defaults to undefined).

## Evidence
- Wall-clock proof demonstrates the mechanism: `retryAsync` without `sleepWithAbort` takes 1502ms to notice an abort fired at 50ms; with `sleepWithAbort`, it notices in ~51ms.
- The signal is threaded end-to-end from the public API (`resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) through `bootstrap-files.ts` → `bootstrap-cache.ts` → `workspace.ts` to the internal retry helpers.
- `sleepWithAbort` is well-tested in `@openclaw/retry` and used by 10+ call sites across the codebase.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (bare setTimeout, no signal)
```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-workspace-retry-abort.mjs
=== BEFORE (bare setTimeout, no signal) ===
{
  "elapsedMs": 1502,
  "calls": 2,
  "verdict": "FAIL: abort did not interrupt backoff"
}
```
Abort fired at ~50ms; the retry still waited the full 1500ms backoff and attempted a 2nd call.

### After (sleepWithAbort)
```bash
=== AFTER (sleepWithAbort) ===
{
  "elapsedMs": 51,
  "calls": 1,
  "verdict": "PASS: abort interrupted backoff immediately"
}
```
Same abort timing; the backoff was interrupted in ~1ms and no retry was attempted.

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- New regression test in `src/agents/workspace.test.ts`: "aborts promptly during retry backoff when the caller signal fires" — verifies abort interrupts the retry delay with fake timers and confirms timer cleanup
- Existing workspace tests unchanged — the optional signal parameter is backward-compatible

target.title: fix(plugins): validate pattern-based and conditional config schemas
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin config schemas with an empty explicit `properties` map were classified as empty even when `patternProperties`, `dependentSchemas`, or an active `if` plus `then`/`else` conditional imposed real validation rules. Valid pattern-keyed plugin configuration could therefore be rejected as “config must be empty,” while active conditional constraints could be skipped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The empty-schema shortcut now recognizes pattern and dependency constraints and only treats conditionals as active when `if` is paired with `then` or `else`. Standalone `if`, `then`, and `else` remain on the empty-config path because JSON Schema gives them no independent validation effect.

The implementation was checked against the repository's actual validator dependency, TypeBox 1.3.3: its coverage table and compiler source support `patternProperties`, `dependentSchemas`, and `if/then/else`, and its conditional engine defaults missing branches to `true`.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can use pattern-keyed and active conditional config schemas without the loader incorrectly requiring an empty config. Semantically inactive standalone conditional keywords do not bypass the empty-config guard.

target.title: improve(diagnostics): surface run startup phases as session-correlated events
target.body:
Closes #107981

## What Problem This Solves

The embedded-agent runner reports useful startup milestones through an internal callback, but public diagnostic subscribers cannot currently observe them. That leaves status surfaces and diagnostics extensions unable to distinguish context assembly from the first model call while a turn is starting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the public additive diagnostic event `run.execution_phase` with the existing run/session correlation fields and the runner's phase payload. The runner entry wraps `onExecutionPhase` once, emits through the public asynchronous diagnostic lane, preserves any existing callback, and tracks session-ID rotation so later phases remain correctly correlated.

The diagnostic stability recorder and diagnostics-otel extension recognize the new event. The plugin SDK type is public like the existing run-attempt and run-progress event types. Documentation explicitly treats diagnostic event kinds as additive and tells external consumers to keep a default branch rather than assume exhaustive event-kind handling.

## User Impact

Diagnostics consumers can now show meaningful turn-startup progress without subscribing to an internal control-UI path. The public diagnostics bus already serves third-party OTel integrations; this event adds phase names and correlation IDs, not prompt or response content. Existing callbacks and consumers retain their behavior; diagnostics-disabled processes emit nothing.

target.title: feat(feeds): add local marketplace watches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signed marketplace feeds can be refreshed and inspected, but users cannot durably watch individual entries or review verified changes later. That leaves update awareness as a manual full-catalog comparison.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first client-side watch slice described by the feeds notification plan:

- durable local plugin watches and bounded update history in shared SQLite schema v4
- verified refresh materialization for version/install, removal, blocked, and publisher/security-state changes
- per-watch accepted baselines so unsigned intermediate writes and skipped sequences cannot lose changes
- source binding by feed ID and URL, plus idempotent read/dismiss and functional mute behavior
- `plugins marketplace watch ...` and `plugins marketplace updates ...` operator commands

Only accepted signed plugin feeds can create or advance watches. The schema keeps `item_kind` generic for skills, but this PR does not claim skill watches before a signed skill-feed producer exists.

## User Impact

Users can watch a marketplace plugin, refresh its signed feed normally, list verified local updates, and mark those updates read or dismissed. Muted watches keep their trusted baseline current without producing update events. History is bounded to 500 watches and 500 updates.

This remains local client state. It does not add a hosted inbox, push delivery, polling daemon, or server-side notification service.

## Evidence

- 80 shared-state and schema migration tests
- 51 doctor/state migration tests
- 50 marketplace, signed-feed, and watch-store tests
- 6 lazy CLI routing tests

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior is unchanged: each warning still fires exactly once. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows the same pattern from #101746 and #109000.

## User Impact

Long-running gateways no longer accumulate unbounded memory from one-shot warning dedup caches. Warning behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/plugins/provider-validation.ts` — deprecated discovery provider warnings
- `src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.ts` — flat streaming key deprecation
- `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.ts` — deprecated config API warnings

target.title: fix(polls): reject polls with fewer than two options
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where plugin poll actions with fewer than two options could receive a `maxSelections` value greater than the number of available options. The helper returned `2` for zero- and one-option multiselect polls, allowing an impossible poll state to travel farther into channel delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared public SDK helper now enforces the same minimum-two-options invariant as `normalizePollInput`. Invalid polls fail immediately with the established `Poll requires at least 2 options` error; valid single-select and multiselect behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and bundled Discord/Telegram poll actions now get one consistent, actionable error for invalid option counts instead of an invalid selection limit. Polls with two or more options behave exactly as before.

## Compatibility Evidence

`resolvePollMaxSelections` was introduced on 2026-07-16 in `16c14e5bbfc9e3a82203272ec7bb82b586df0a84`. No version tag (`v*`) contains that commit; the latest shipped tag is `v2026.7.1`, which predates the helper. The invalid-input return behavior is therefore not a shipped public SDK contract.

Final-head callers were checked:

- Core outbound already rejects fewer than two poll options before calling the helper.
- Discord and Telegram action runtimes pass their parsed answer-array lengths directly; rejecting 0/1 there gives the same minimum-two-options contract as `normalizePollInput` instead of sending an impossible poll.
- The SDK export has no public documentation promising permissive behavior for invalid option counts.

## Evidence

Exact PR head `965b73d948c6c3628cacf2991104c06c9518d440`, importing the public SDK helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-actions`:

```text
0/true: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
1/true: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
0/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
1/false: error=Poll requires at least 2 options
2/true: result=2
5/true: result=5

exact_head=965b73d948c6c3628cacf2991104c06c9518d440
```

target.title: improve: index transcript mirror persistence checks
target.body:
Stacked child of #110374. The GitHub base is intentionally `josh/clawdbot-d02.1.9.1.40-db6-generation-cursors`; merge or rebase the parent first.

AI-assisted: implemented with Codex. I reviewed the implementation, ran the repository autoreview workflow to a clean result, and verified the exact production owners against current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex and Copilot transcript mirrors decode every event in a session while holding the session writer lock just to recover idempotency facts, persisted user rows, and Codex message sequencing. A small mirror batch therefore allocates and parses in proportion to the full transcript, including on 100,000-message sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing v12 transcript identity indexes from #110374 already own the required facts. This child adds only three typed writer-lock reads: supplied-key existence, supplied-key user messages, and the exact indexed message-event count. Codex and Copilot prepare candidate keys before acquiring the lock and query only those facts. No schema, HTTP/SSE, active-memory, cache, raw SQL surface, or generic query abstraction is added.

## User Impact

Large Codex and Copilot sessions can mirror a small batch without decoding the complete transcript under the writer lock. Dedupe identity, gateway user correlation, hooks, sequence assignment, append/update publication, and replacement behavior remain unchanged.

## Changes Walkthrough

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.types.ts` | Adds three narrow writer facts |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-store.ts` | Implements batched indexed Kysely reads |
| `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts` | Binds facts to writer ownership |
| `src/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime.ts` | Projects typed plugin-safe facts |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts` | Replaces full mirror-state scan |
| `extensions/copilot/src/dual-write-transcripts.ts` | Replaces full key scan |
| `src/plugin-sdk/session-transcript-runtime.test.ts` | Proves batching and replacement reset |
| `src/state/sqlite-query-plan.test.ts` | Pins identity/count index plans |
| `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.test.ts` | Proves concurrent Codex dedupe |
| `extensions/copilot/src/dual-write-transcripts.test.ts` | Proves concurrent Copilot dedupe |
| `scripts/bench-transcript-mirrors.ts` | Adds reproducible production-owner benchmark |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime.md` | Documents indexed write-lock facts |

## Evidence

### Apples-to-apples benchmark

Both revisions ran in clean detached worktrees on the same Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kxstq13f2qjb6gbktd89njcc` (Linux 6.6.141 x64, Node v24.18.0). The identical candidate benchmark file invoked the real `codexTranscriptMirrorRuntime.mirror` and `dualWriteCopilotTranscriptBestEffort` owners. The harness rejects a supplied source SHA unless it equals the checkout's actual `HEAD`.

- Baseline: current fetched `origin/main` at `923d92bdd0e3ddb978ab566efe29a737dc204edf`
- Candidate: `7a9e6db40674118c235c5baf6fb6aa8aceb8abaa`

- Operation: four supplied messages, two existing and two new
- Warmup/runs: 2 warmups, 12 measured runs per mirror/revision
- Timing: end-to-end owner latency; in this uncontended run it includes lock acquisition/hold and any post-lock publication, so lock hold was not separately instrumented
- Allocation proxy: process `resourceUsage().maxRSS` growth after fixture seeding

| Mirror | Revision | Median | p95 | Max RSS growth |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Codex | current main | 787.916 ms | 827.691 ms | 1,057,688 KiB |
| Codex | candidate | 46.422 ms | 48.570 ms | 2,048 KiB |
| Copilot | current main | 769.497 ms | 827.412 ms | 1,202,856 KiB |

Candidate reduction: Codex median 94.11% (16.97x), p95 94.13% (17.04x), RSS proxy 99.81%; Copilot median 94.37% (17.75x), p95 94.70% (18.88x), RSS proxy 99.85%.

<details>
<summary>Raw latency samples (milliseconds)</summary>

```text
main Codex:     750.449, 820.000, 818.584, 778.525, 797.308, 802.771, 774.695, 726.949, 803.639, 740.711, 827.691, 754.341
```

Current main decodes 100,000 transcript payloads per operation to build mirror state. Candidate Copilot decodes zero existing transcript payloads for supplied-key existence. Candidate Codex decodes only the one matching persisted user payload in this fixture; its exact message count reads the covering `(session_id, event_type, seq DESC)` identity index without decoding event JSON. Supplied-key queries are batched at 900 keys and seek through `idx_agent_transcript_message_idempotency`; joined user rows use the transcript-event primary key.

### Correctness and contracts

- 63 focused tests passed across SDK facts, query plans, Codex, and Copilot.
- Coverage includes replacement/current-generation reset, >999 supplied keys, exact raw message count, persisted user recovery, concurrent same-key mirrors, hooks, updates, and sequence behavior.
- Query plans prohibit transcript table scans for supplied-key lookups and pin `idx_agent_transcript_message_idempotency`, `idx_agent_transcript_event_sequence`, and the transcript-event primary key.
- Final autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Personally inspected official Codex at `2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3`:

target.title: fix(browser): time out download saves
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser download waits used the configured timeout only until Playwright emitted the download event. After that event, the timer was cleared before `download.saveAs(...)` ran, so a stalled save could leave the browser tool call hanging indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The download capture now removes the event listener when the download is observed, but keeps the original deadline active until the save operation settles. If the save hangs, the same timeout rejects the tool call instead of waiting forever.

## User Impact

Browser download tools now fail with the configured timeout when the browser starts a download but Playwright cannot finish saving it, making stalled downloads recoverable for agents and users.

## Evidence

- Current head `e1bab3bd8458e35c71c452d092ed5111c48be881` passed `Real behavior proof` on GitHub Actions run `29630696107`.
- Current head `e1bab3bd8458e35c71c452d092ed5111c48be881` passed `check-lint` on GitHub Actions run `29630528905`.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Real browser download proof on Node `v24.18.0` with Playwright Chromium exercised the current `createDownloadCaptureForPage` implementation. It first saved a normal real download, then patched the real Playwright `Download.saveAs(...)` for a second real download so the save phase never settled. target.title: fix(mattermost): preserve websocket posts across restarts
target.body:
Related: #109657

## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost WebSocket `posted` events were detached from the socket and protected only by a five-minute in-memory replay guard. If OpenClaw restarted after receiving a frame but before adopting its turn, the post was lost because Mattermost reconnects do not replay already-received posts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost plugin now durably admits every raw `posted` envelope before scheduling its handler, using `post.id` as the event identity. Channel lanes honor channel IDs from `post.channel_id`, envelope `data.channel_id`, and broadcast metadata so inspection and claiming preserve ordering for every supported event shape.

The shared ingress drain owns restart recovery, per-lane ordering, bounded retry/dead-letter behavior, deferred debounce claims, and merged-turn adoption fan-out. The five-minute replay guard is deleted after parity through 30-day, 20,000-entry completion tombstones. Admissions are serialized so append retries cannot invert same-channel order; shutdown waits for admitted work and closes the prune/pump race.

Cold-gap limitation: Mattermost does not replay posts missed while OpenClaw is disconnected. This change protects frames OpenClaw received and durably admitted; it does not fill that platform-level gap. Persistent admission failures terminate the WebSocket loudly instead of silently losing later posts.

## User Impact

Mattermost posts accepted by OpenClaw now survive process restarts and dispatch once after recovery. Operators also get durable duplicate rejection within the bounded retention window and loud failure when the ingress store cannot accept new posts.

## Evidence

- Mattermost suite: 620 tests green.
- Focused ingress matrix: 16 tests green, including raw-envelope persistence, restart recovery, completion dedupe, all three channel-id shapes, same-lane admission order, retry/escalation, shutdown/prune behavior, and deferred merged adoption.
- Dead-code export and unused-file gates: zero findings.
- Final branch head: `8d98b23e99addeb84d4144fba60cb3ffd6698f2b`.

AI-assisted; maintainer-reviewed and understood.

target.title: fix(pairing): normalize account key in legacy allowFrom filename parsing
target.body:
Closes #110187

## What Problem This Solves

The startup-migration gate refuses to report the gateway ready when a legacy allowFrom JSON file has a non-canonical account id segment in its filename (e.g. `telegram-HY_RIN_Bot-allowFrom.json` instead of `telegram-hy_rin_bot-allowFrom.json`). The `parseAllowFromFilename` parser cannot match it to any configured account, leaving the file unresolved. The file is never deleted, so every restart produces the same migration warning — a permanent crash loop with no in-product recovery path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`parseAllowFromFilename` compared the raw filename segment (`accountKey`) against `safeAccountKey(accountId)` without normalizing the segment first. The write path has always used `safeAccountKey` (lowercase + special-char replacement) to generate filenames, but the migration reader was not updated to apply the same normalization when parsing them. Codex review (July 17–18) on the linked issue confirmed: the parser mismatch is still present on current main, and `#108453` (default-account fallback) did not cover mixed-case or non-canonical account id spellings.

## User Impact

- Users upgrading with a legacy allowFrom file whose account segment is not in canonical `safeAccountKey` form no longer crash-loop
- The file is successfully migrated to SQLite and removed; no manual intervention needed
- Previously-working canonical filenames (e.g. `telegram-hy_rin_bot-allowFrom.json`) continue to resolve identically — `safeAccountKey` is idempotent on already-normalized inputs
- Ambiguous cases (two configured account ids that collide under `safeAccountKey`) remain unresolved with the same warning — no behavior change
- Non-canonical DEFAULT filenames (e.g. `telegram-DEFAULT-allowFrom.json`) remain unresolved — the implicit bundled-default fallback stays restricted to the literal canonical suffix

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.15.0, branch `fix/allowfrom-accountkey-normalize-110187`, SHA `ee67b5a882`

### End-to-end `autoMigrateLegacyState` proof

This exercises the same migration entry point used by `openclaw doctor --fix` and gateway startup (`src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts:586`).

**Scenario A: mixed-case HY_RIN_Bot + canonical default → gateway can report READY**

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module
import { autoMigrateLegacyState } from "./src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts";
// ... setup: telegram-HY_RIN_Bot-allowFrom.json + telegram-default-allowFrom.json on disk
// ... config: channels.telegram.accounts = { hy_rin_bot: { token: "REDACTED" } }

const result = await autoMigrateLegacyState({ cfg: config, env, homedir: () => stateDir });

=== SCENARIO A: mixed-case HY_RIN_Bot + canonical default ===
Changes: [
  "Migrated 2 telegram/hy_rin_bot allowFrom entries → shared SQLite state",
  "Migrated 1 telegram/default allowFrom entry → shared SQLite state"
]
Warnings: (none)
HY_RIN_Bot removed: ✅
default removed: ✅
Gateway can report READY: ✅
```

**Scenario B: uppercase DEFAULT → file left in place, unresolved warning blocks readiness**

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module
import { autoMigrateLegacyState } from "./src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts";
// ... setup: telegram-DEFAULT-allowFrom.json on disk
// ... config: channels.telegram.accounts = { my_bot: { token: "REDACTED" } }

const result = await autoMigrateLegacyState({ cfg: config, env, homedir: () => stateDir });

=== SCENARIO B: uppercase DEFAULT ===
Changes: []
Warnings: [ "Legacy channel allowFrom channel/account is unresolved; left in place" ]
DEFAULT left in place: ✅
Has channel-pairing warning: ✅
```

### Scenario Matrix

Filename segment | Configured accounts | `safeAccountKey(segment)` | Expected | Result
---|---|---|---|---
`hy_rin_bot` (canonical) | `["hy_rin_bot"]` | `hy_rin_bot` | MATCH → `hy_rin_bot` | ✅
`HY_RIN_Bot` (mixed-case, #110187) | `["hy_rin_bot"]` | `hy_rin_bot` | MATCH → `hy_rin_bot` | ✅
`My_Work_Bot` (underscore-bearing mixed-case) | `["my_work_bot"]` | `my_work_bot` | MATCH → `my_work_bot` | ✅
`default` (no config) | `[]` | `default` | MATCH via fallback (literal `accountKey === "default"`) | ✅
`DEFAULT` (uppercase, no config) | `[]` | `default` | UNRESOLVED (non-canonical default guarded) | ✅
`ops_bot` (ambiguous collision) | `["ops/bot", "ops_bot"]` | `ops_bot` | AMBIGUOUS (file kept) | ✅
`unknown` (unrelated) | `["hy_rin_bot"]` | `unknown` | UNRESOLVED (file kept) | ✅
`(empty)` (pathological) | `["hy_rin_bot"]` | (throw) | SKIP (safe, no throw) | ✅

### Test output (9 channel-pairing migration tests, all pass)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.test.ts --run

 ✓ |infra| src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.test.ts (9 tests) 1385ms
     ✓ imports pairing requests and scoped allowFrom entries into SQLite
     ✓ imports a built-in channel's explicit default account without channel config
     ✓ merges with authoritative SQLite rows and keeps unreadable sources
     ✓ leaves ambiguous sanitized account filenames in place
     ✓ does not infer default accounts for external channels
     ✓ imports allowFrom files with mixed-case account id segments
     ✓ imports underscore-bearing allowFrom files with mixed-case account id segments
     ✓ leaves uppercase DEFAULT allowFrom files unresolved for bundled channels
     ✓ leaves overlapping channel and account filename interpretations in place

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Codex Review Resolution (July 18)

Finding | Status | Change
---|---|---
Legacy filename contract unverified on current main | ✅ Confirmed | Code archaeology across 6 commits: all write paths use `safeAccountKey`; read path was missing it
Accept the historical raw account-id spelling alongside the canonical safe key | ✅ Fixed | `safeAccountKey(accountKey)` normalizes both raw and canonical spellings before comparing
Ambiguity left unresolved and explicitly reported, not guessed | ✅ Preserved | `matchingAccountIds.length > 1` → ambiguous logic unchanged
Overly broad normalization could associate a legacy allowlist file with the wrong account | ✅ Safe | `safeAccountKey` deterministic; collision → ambiguous (file kept); `removeImportedSource` only on successful match
Whether raw legacy filenames are an intentional supported input | ✅ Addressed | Not intentional, but migration code reads user disk files; not tolerating causes permanent crash loop
Whether a matching state migration already landed | ✅ Verified | Only `5e41074009` (#108453) — different root cause
Add focused regression coverage for mixed-case and underscore-bearing Telegram account IDs | ✅ Added | 3 new tests
**[P1] Keep implicit default fallback canonical** — `normalizedAccountKey === DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID` broadened attribution | ✅ Fixed | Changed to `accountKey === DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID` + guard non-canonical DEFAULT segments: when `safeAccountKey` maps a non-literal-default segment to `"default"`, skip the filter so the file stays unresolved
**[P1] Needs real behavior proof** — no Doctor/gateway-startup evidence | ✅ Added | `autoMigrateLegacyState` end-to-end: Scenario A shows mixed-case file migrated, removed, zero warnings → gateway can report READY; Scenario B shows uppercase DEFAULT left in place with unresolved warning

### Gateway startup crash-loop path (code trace)

1. `parseAllowFromFilename` returns `{ target: null, reason: "unresolved" }` — `src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.ts:139`
2. `migrateLegacyChannelPairingState` pushes warning — `src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.ts:271-274`
3. `channelPairing.warnings` merged into `autoMigrateLegacyState` result — `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts:1265`
4. `noteStartupStateMigrationResult` pushes into `startupMigrationWarnings` — `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts:413`
5. `startupMigrationWarnings.length > 0` → `throwStartupMigrationRefusal` — `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts:624-630`
6. File is not deleted (unresolved → `continue`), so `hasLegacy: files.length > 0` is true on next restart — `src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.ts:71`

## What Changed

**`src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.ts`** (+24/-8):

- Normalize `accountKey` via `safeAccountKey` before comparing with configured account ids
- Wrap in try/catch so pathological filename segments skip safely instead of throwing
- Guard non-canonical DEFAULT segments: when `safeAccountKey` maps a non-literal-default segment (e.g. `"DEFAULT"`) to `"default"`, skip the filter so the file remains unresolved rather than being attributed to the implicit default account and deleted
- Keep implicit bundled-default fallback on the literal canonical suffix (`accountKey === DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID`)

**`src/infra/state-migrations.channel-pairing.test.ts`** (+62):

- Added `imports allowFrom files with mixed-case account id segments` — `telegram-HY_RIN_Bot-allowFrom.json` + configured `hy_rin_bot`
- Added `imports underscore-bearing allowFrom files with mixed-case account id segments` — `telegram-My_Work_Bot-allowFrom.json` + configured `my_work_bot`
- Added `leaves uppercase DEFAULT allowFrom files unresolved for bundled channels` — `telegram-DEFAULT-allowFrom.json` with no configured accounts → file kept in place

## What Did NOT Change

- `detectLegacyChannelPairingState` (detection logic, `accountIds` normalization via `resolveAllowFromAccountId`)
- Ambiguity detection (`matchingAccountIds.length > 1` → ambiguous, file kept in place)
- Default-account fallback for bundled channels (`CHANNEL_IDS` + literal `DEFAULT_ACCOUNT_ID` check)
- `migrateLegacyChannelPairingState` callers (4 call sites in `state-migrations.doctor.ts`)
- `removeImportedSource` (only called on successful match, unchanged)
- Startup gate severity (warnings remain fatal — separate concern per #109073)
- Other legacy file types (pairing files, plugin state sidecars, session stores)

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Normalizing `accountKey` via `safeAccountKey` for configured-account matching is the narrowest safe change, while guarding non-canonical DEFAULT segments prevents the implicit default fallback from being broadened. Codex review confirmed: "Normalize filename segments only for configured-account matching; keep the implicit bundled default fallback restricted to the literal canonical default suffix."
- **Refactor needed**: No.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(cli): show clean errors for missing input files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three CLI input paths exposed raw Node.js `ENOENT` text when the user supplied a missing file:

- `openclaw config set --batch-file <path>`
- `openclaw config patch --file <path>`
- `openclaw secrets apply --from <path>`

The raw filesystem error is noisy and less actionable than naming the flag and user-supplied path.

## Solution

- Translate only `ENOENT` at each command-owned file-read boundary using the shared `hasErrnoCode` guard.
- Preserve the original error as `cause`; rethrow every non-`ENOENT` failure unchanged.
- Use a typed local missing-plan error so secrets rendering suppresses only that expected raw cause. Unrelated apply errors, including ones with similar message text, retain their diagnostic causes.

## Behavior

The three commands now exit 1 with these messages:

```text
Error: --batch-file not found: /tmp/missing-batch.json5
Error: --file not found: /tmp/missing-patch.json5
Secrets apply failed: Secrets plan file not found: /tmp/missing-plan.json. Re-run openclaw secrets apply --from <path> --dry-run to inspect the plan without writing.
```

No parse, config write, or secrets apply operation runs after the missing input is detected.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxstbgzscnwa3jeeqyr62j8h`: `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts` — 160 passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users filtering oc-path results with numeric predicates could match non-decimal values when the predicate or source value used JavaScript-coercible forms such as hexadecimal, exponent notation, or blank strings.

## Why This Change Was Made

## User Impact

Users can rely on numeric oc-path filters to compare only decimal numeric values, avoiding surprising matches from loosely coerced strings while preserving normal decimal comparisons.

target.title: fix: prevent dev watch rebuild loops after live git pulls
target.body:
Closes #110420

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers running source-tree dev watch could enter a continuous rebuild loop after pulling a change that added or updated a generated extension asset.

The watcher could treat build output as source, interrupt the build before its stamps completed, and repeatedly rebuild until manually stopped.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extension asset build hooks now declare their source-tree outputs, and watch exclusions are derived from that metadata instead of a fixed path list. The watcher refreshes this metadata before every child start so live source updates cannot leave it using stale classifications.

Text-based asset builders also avoid rewriting identical output, preventing unnecessary filesystem events outside the watcher.

## User Impact

Dev watch now performs one rebuild and restart after a relevant live source update instead of reacting to its own generated files.

No-op asset builds preserve output timestamps. Normal source changes continue to trigger rebuilds and restarts.

## Evidence

- Focused Browser, diffs, Discord, metadata-classification, runtime-postbuild, and watcher tests passed.
- Real Browser, Discord, and diffs asset builds were run twice; the second run preserved every generated output timestamp.
- Every current extension asset build hook is covered by the generated-output contract.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed in a Blacksmith Testbox.
- `pnpm build` passed in the same Testbox.
- The full build completed in 87.1 seconds, including one successful bundled asset build phase.
