target.title: fix(zalouser): settle waitForExit when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup could leave channel shutdown waiting forever. This happened when the gateway stop signal was already aborted before the monitor registered its listener, or became aborted while startup allowlist/group resolution was in progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`AbortSignal` does not replay an `abort` event to listeners registered after the signal has fired. The monitor now checks for shutdown before asynchronous startup work and rechecks after that work before creating the Zalo listener. The existing listener lifecycle remains local to listener startup; no extra lifecycle state is introduced.

The fix stays inside the ZaloUser plugin and adds no config, protocol, SDK, or dependency surface.

## User Impact

ZaloUser stop and restart operations now settle promptly instead of hanging during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions. An aborted startup also avoids restoring a Zalo listener session.

## Evidence

The committed tests exercise the real `monitorZalouserProvider` function with only the Zalo API/listener boundary mocked:

- A pre-aborted signal skips startup API calls and never calls `startZaloListener`.
- A signal aborted while the friends lookup Promise is pending completes startup resolution but never calls `startZaloListener`.
- Existing mutable allowlist and group-name startup resolution remains covered.

Focused validation on head `86bb679c6f`:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       25 passed (25)
```

Command:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.group-gating.test.ts extensions/zalouser/src/monitor.account-scope.test.ts
```

The platform contract is also directly observable in Node: adding an `abort` listener after `AbortController.abort()` does not invoke that listener, while checking `signal.aborted` catches the state synchronously.

A configured ZaloUser account is not available in this environment, so the evidence stops at the production monitor with the external Zalo boundary mocked. Maintainers may either run the same stop/restart scenario with a configured account or explicitly accept this focused boundary proof.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenCode Zen users could not discover or resolve the `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol` models even though OpenCode's live model catalog already advertised them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-owned Zen catalog now includes the three live GPT-5.6 routes with their OpenCode routing, context/output limits, pricing tiers, and supported reasoning efforts. The OpenCode thinking policy also exposes those declared `xhigh` and `max` levels while leaving proxied Claude profiles unchanged.

## User Impact

OpenCode Zen users can now see and select all three GPT-5.6 tiers through OpenClaw model discovery, including when the static catalog fallback is used, without `xhigh` or `max` being silently clamped to `high`.

## Evidence

- Third-party live red: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` returned `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol`; the OpenClaw live catalog contract failed with those exact three IDs reported as missing static metadata.
- Credentialed third-party live suite: both OpenCode live tests passed, covering catalog alignment plus a real tool-call/reasoning replay through the provider.
- Credentialed OpenClaw CLI E2E: `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, and `gpt-5.6-sol` were each invoked with `--thinking max` through `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses`; all calls returned HTTP 200 with reasoning-token usage and `aborted: false`.
- OpenClaw CLI E2E on the final commit: the repository source completed its TypeScript and bundled-plugin build, then `models list --provider opencode --json` returned 55 models including all three GPT-5.6 routes with 1,050,000-token context windows. The command used isolated OpenClaw state directories.
- Review reproduction red: both the bundled public policy artifact and registered provider surface silently omitted `xhigh`/`max` for the new GPT-5.6 routes; focused tests failed 2 cases.
- Review fix green: the same focused policy tests passed 18/18, including `max` remaining available with the provider-owned profile.
- OpenCode extension suite: 5 files, 35/35 tests passed.
- Extension source and extension-test typechecks passed.
- Targeted oxlint, oxfmt check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- After ClawSweeper review, the focused public-policy test was simplified to use only the fields needed by the assertion; its focused test and the extension test-type lane passed again.
- The aggregate `check:changed` wrapper could not reach its checks because its delegated Testbox dependency install hit the host's file-descriptor limit while fetching unrelated optional platform packages; the corresponding scoped typecheck/lint/test lanes above were run directly. Full hosted gates remain owned by PR CI.

All CLI and live verification used the OpenClaw repository source; it did not invoke Co-Claw.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in parity tool-call fetch
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109991

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok HTTP responses in the QA Lab runtime parity tool-call fetch. This drains/cancels the unread response body to free the connection immediately instead of waiting for GC.
**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When the QA Lab runtime parity endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (e.g. 400, 503), the response body stream is left unconsumed. In long-running agent sessions this leaks connections and can degrade reliability.

**Root Cause**: The early `return null` on line 1054 of `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts` exits without cancelling or reading the response body. The runtime holds the stream open until GC, which is non-deterministic.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null. This explicitly signals to the runtime that the body stream is unwanted, immediately freeing the underlying TCP connection back to the pool. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guards against the cancel() promise rejecting in environments where the stream is already locked, errored, or in a broken state. This pattern is already established across 15+ locations in the codebase (google-oauth, crabline, vault, slack, msteams attachments, claude-code beta verifier, etc.) and is the standard web API approach for discarding unwanted response payloads.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Simulated with Node.js ReadableStream + Response API (same Web API contract used by the fetch runtime). The pattern is identical to the 15+ existing body-cancel call sites already shipping in production across google-oauth, vault, crabline, slack, msteams, and release scripts.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx scripts/evidence-parity.ts`

**After-fix evidence**:
```
--- Body cancel on error path ---
Body cancel: YES ✅
Error: Parity fetch failed (503)

--- Cancel rejection handled ---
Cancel rejection suppressed: ✅
Error: Parity fetch failed (400)

--- Null body safe ---
Null body: safe ✅

--- Double cancel safe ---
Double cancel safe: ✅ (count=2)

COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 4 tests pass with COMMAND_EXIT_CODE=0: (1) body cancel fires correctly on error path before throwing; (2) cancel rejection is caught and suppressed by `.catch(() => undefined)`, proving the guard works; (3) null body is handled safely via optional chaining without throwing; (4) double cancel works without side effects (count=2, no errors), confirming idempotent behavior.

**What was not tested**: Full integration test against a live target (requires running QA Lab with a configured runtime endpoint). Unit test coverage for the runtime-parity.ts function (the function is integration-level and returns parsed payloads, making the body cancel observable only via connection-pool behavior at scale). The body cancel pattern is well-established and consistent with the rest of the codebase.

---

## merge-risk

Low. One-line addition of a well-established pattern with no configuration changes, no new dependencies, and no impact on the ok response path. The `.catch(() => undefined)` makes it safe even in edge-case stream states.

## Real environment evidence

### 1. Session-catalog: hung-node timeout tests (3/3 passed)

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/anthropic/session-catalog.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "bounds|starts|keeps the underlying"

 ✓ Claude session catalog > bounds how long a hung paired-node catalog can delay the caller 19ms
 ✓ Claude session catalog > starts paired-node discovery while the local catalog is still reading 9ms
 ✓ Claude session catalog > keeps the underlying paired-node list failure 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 24 skipped (27)
```

### 2. Gateway-child: empty baseUrl fix tests (2/2 passed)

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-child.test.ts --reporter=verbose -t "omits empty base|does not copy OpenAI"

```

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109985

Two fixes:
1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message instead of a raw SyntaxError.

## Real behavior proof

### 1. qa-lab response body cancel

**Behavior addressed**: When an HTTP error response (4xx/5xx) was received, `response.json()` was never called but the response body was left unconsumed, holding the connection open.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js test runner (vitest) with mocked `fetch`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Each non-2xx path calls `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, covering:
- All error status codes (400, 403, 429, 500, 503) for both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`
- Null body (safe: optional chaining `?.`)
- Cancel rejection (suppressed by `.catch(() => undefined)`)

**What was not tested**: `postJson` was not modified — it calls `response.json()` on error to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### 2. vertex-adc JSON.parse guard

**Behavior addressed**: Malformed credential files at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` would cause a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, making debugging harder.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js test runner (vitest) with temp malformed credential file.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Observed result after the fix**:

## Summary

**What changed**: Added `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw in `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` error path, so the unread response body stream is cancelled and the underlying connection is released immediately.

**What NOT changed**: No change to any other provider (OpenAI, Bedrock, etc.). No change to success paths. No change to retry or timeout logic. No new dependencies.

Fixes #109978

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` receives a non-OK HTTP response (e.g. 403, 429, 500), the `response.body` readable stream remains unconsumed. Node.js fetch keeps the TCP connection alive until the stream is GC'd or read to completion, causing connection stalls and resource leaks.

**Root Cause**: Missing `response.body.cancel()` in the error path of `downloadGeneratedVideoFromUri` in `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.ts`.

**Solution**: Call `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the error. The optional chaining handles null-body responses gracefully. The `.catch()` ensures the original download error is always thrown even if the cancel itself rejects.

target.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadCronQuarantineFile` in `src/cron/store.ts` reads the cron quarantine sidecar with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A corrupted or hostile quarantine file could force the cron load path to buffer an arbitrarily large file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Quarantine sidecars are small JSON files. An 8 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate quarantine state while preventing the cron load path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector. When the sidecar exceeds the cap during writes, it is archived and a fresh file is started so SQLite persistence continues.

## Changes

1. **Bounded reads**: `loadCronQuarantineFile` uses the shared `readRegularFile` helper with an 8 MiB cap instead of unbounded `fs.promises.readFile`.
2. **Bounded writes**: `saveCronQuarantineFile` checks the serialized payload size before writing. If it exceeds 8 MiB, the existing file is archived and a fresh file with only the new entries is created. If a single entry alone exceeds the cap, writes fail with a clear error.
3. **Archive retention**: Archived sidecar files use unique names (`{path}.{timestamp}.{random}.archive.json`). Up to 5 most recent archives are retained; when a new archive pushes the count past 5, the oldest archives are pruned to prevent unbounded disk growth.
4. **Tests**: Regression coverage for bounded reads, oversized write rejection, archive creation and fresh-start recovery, archive pruning at the retention limit.

## User Impact

A corrupted or oversized quarantine sidecar is rejected before OOM. When the sidecar grows past 8 MiB during cron operations, the overflow is archived and a fresh sidecar is started, keeping cron persistence alive. The last 5 overflow archives are preserved for review; older ones are pruned.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `47bcbd22ab4f0fe4995386a8c8abc6287298af0b`

### Full test suite: 52/52 passed (including SQLite-dependent tests)

```
$ node -v
v24.15.0

$ CI=true node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/store.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |cron| src/cron/store.test.ts (52 tests) 1493ms
     ✓ prunes oldest archives when the retention limit is exceeded  472ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  52 passed (52)
```

All 6 quarantine-specific tests pass (bounded reads, oversized write rejection, archive rotation, fresh-start recovery, single-archive retention, archive pruning). The SQLite-dependent `lets doctor import legacy top-level array jobs into SQLite and archive the source` test also passes.

### Neighboring cron suites: 62/62 passed

### Archive retention proof

`prunes oldest archives when the retention limit is exceeded` — writes 7 oversized sidecars in sequence, each triggering archive rotation, then asserts that at most 5 archives remain. The two oldest archives are pruned.

target.title: fix(cron): stop a cron job's own marker from blocking its awaited wake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A `wakeMode: "now"` main-session cron job installs its active execution marker before awaiting `runHeartbeatOnce`. The heartbeat admission guard then sees cron work in progress and can reject the wake that the job itself owns. The cron path falls back to an asynchronous request and records success before delivery is confirmed.

This is a deterministic defect found while investigating #105257. It fixes an adjacent, reproducible self-block; it does not claim to close that broader intermittent report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron path now passes its exact active marker `{ jobId, token }` through the internal Gateway heartbeat adapter. The heartbeat runner bypasses only that still-current marker:

- another cron job still blocks the wake;
- a same-ID replacement marker still blocks the stale owner;
- an absent or stale owner keeps the previous busy behavior;
- queued `cron.run` work cannot deadlock on its own `CommandLane.Cron` entry;
- the public plugin heartbeat facade cannot supply or forge internal ownership.

The exact token matters. Discounting by job ID alone would allow a superseded execution to claim ownership of a newer run.

## User Impact

Main-session `wakeMode: "now"` cron runs now wait for their owned heartbeat delivery before recording terminal success. Other cron work continues to enforce the existing admission fence. No config, storage, protocol, or public plugin API changes.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage exercises the full decision surface:

- exact marker, unrelated marker, same-ID replacement, and stale replacement;
- direct manual run, Gateway-queued `cron.run`, and natural scheduled firing;
- real heartbeat runner integration and Gateway adapter forwarding;
- owned Cron-lane pressure versus unowned busy behavior;
- marker and command-lane cleanup before sandbox deletion.

Results:

- 88 focused tests passed across cron active jobs, timer/service, Gateway adapter, and heartbeat runner.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed on Blacksmith Testbox ([run 29629429145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29629429145)).
- Fresh autoreview found no actionable issue.

Live proof used the official OpenAI API with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, an isolated QA state root, and a custom loopback Gateway port (`41103`):

- Natural timer: outbound delivery `1784347997662`, terminal success `1784347997665`.
- Real Gateway `cron.run`: outbound delivery `1784348000474`, terminal success `1784348000476`.
- Both successful one-shots were deleted.

The timestamp ordering is the regression oracle: the old self-block records terminal success before the later asynchronous outbound message; the fixed path delivers first.

## Scope

`next-heartbeat` remains asynchronous by design. Issue #105257 remains open for its intermittent payload-loss report.

---

🤖 AI-assisted: original contributor fix reviewed and rewritten with maintainer tests, changed-gate proof, and live OpenAI Gateway verification.

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout in `finally`.
- Added `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts` exercising the real fetch path against a local HTTP server (not a fetch mock): stalled responses abort after the bound; normal 200 responses still resolve.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts`
- The stall cases use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(15_000)` to fire the AbortController watchdog without waiting in real time, then assert the call rejects.

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
 - aborts a stalled putNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging  (pass)
 - aborts a stalled importNostrProfile after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal putNostrProfile round trip                  (pass)
 - still resolves a normal importNostrProfile round trip                (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the server accepting the connection but never ending the response, both helpers reject (AbortError) after the 15s bound instead of remaining pending. With the server returning 200 JSON, both helpers resolve and return `{ ok: true, persisted: true }`, so ordinary profile operations are unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real Nostr relay was not executed (no relay credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

_Status note:_ #106778 has since been closed by #108042, a **consumer-side** guard in the Codex extension (skip retirement on a provable cross-key handoff). The **producer** still emits the misleading parent-terminal `session_end` for every hook-enabled child on current main; this PR fixes that contract at the source — see the live A/B/C evidence below. The two are complementary.


## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.
- **Main reset-in-place** emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier; a dashboard session is replaced via `sessions.reset` (which retires its binding in place), never a create-succession.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

This is behavior-preserving vs the previous revision — the only path that emitted parent `session_end` (explicit `tui-*` successor) still does — while removing the fragile key-shape heuristic from the decision. Because succession is now opt-in, any out-of-tree caller that relied on *implicit* succession via an explicit key runs parallel until it declares `succeedsParent` (the safe direction: a not-retired parent can still be reset; a wrongly-retired one is broken).

**Changed in this revision:** replaced the `startsWith("dashboard:")` key-shape gate with the caller-declared `succeedsParent` flag + a boundary validation — addressing the standing P1 that the emit decision should be an explicit disposition, not a key-shape inference.

**Maintainer note.** The contract question — which Control UI / TUI creations *replace* the selected parent vs run alongside it — is genuinely a maintainer decision (given the #78215 lifecycle provenance, likely @BunsDev). This PR implements the recommended "explicit disposition" shape and preserves today's dispositions; a different contract (an enum, a different default) is a small adjustment.

Scope note: sibling issue #105817 (rejected *oversized* fork retires parent binding) is a **separate** path — fork-size rejection returns before this emit block — and is not addressed here.

## Evidence

### Live Codex-backed A/B/C run (real standalone gateway + codex app-server 0.144.4 + real model turns)

A single run per tree, same harness on three trees (Ubuntu VPS, Node v24.18.0): an **ephemeral standalone gateway** (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --bind loopback --auth token`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/workspace per tree, agent-scoped isolated `CODEX_HOME`, prepared OpenAI OAuth profile — redacted). Parent = the agent main session (`agent:main:main`). Turns are real `gpt-5.5` completions through the managed Codex app-server runtime, driven via the gateway `agent` + `agent.wait` RPC. Dashboard child creation uses the **exact Control-UI "New Chat" payload**: `sessions.create {parentSessionKey, emitCommandHooks:true}` (key omitted → the gateway mints `agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>`). After each step the Codex session-binding rows (plugin state, namespace `app-server-thread-bindings`) are dumped from SQLite.

**Built-in emission detector.** This PR's tree does **not** contain #108042 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms), so its Codex consumer is the old handler that retires the binding on **any** terminal parent `session_end` — and the rollover step below proves that detector live (the binding *is* retired when the event fires). Therefore, the parent binding surviving the detached-child create on this tree is direct evidence that **the producer emitted no terminal event**, with no extra instrumentation.

| Step | **A** — baseline before either fix (`5afb1fb3`, pre-#108042 & pre-this-PR) | **B** — this PR (`0b7e68e1`, no #108042) | **C** — current main (`63b0cac9`, #108042, no this-PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parent turn 1 | ✅ ok — binding `{"state":"active","threadId":…}` | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| Create dashboard child (New-Chat payload) | 💥 **parent binding tombstoned**: `{"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}` | ✅ binding **intact** (`active`, same threadId) | ✅ binding intact |
| Parent turn 2 | 💥 **fails at the durable generation fence**: `Codex session generation is no longer current: <sessionId>` | ✅ **ok — the original parent still works** | ✅ ok |
| Turn in a fresh session | ✅ ok (new sessions work while the parent stays broken — matches the failure #106778 reports) | ✅ ok | ✅ ok |
| `sessions.create {key:"tui-…", succeedsParent:true}` | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` (contract is new in this PR) | ✅ accepted — **parent binding retired (genuine rollover)**; a real turn in the successor session (`sessionKey agent:main:tui-e2e-rollover`) then completes | ❌ rejected: `unexpected property 'succeedsParent'` |

**Tri-state contract, proven live on the PR tree** (each parent first completed a real turn, so its binding was `active`; the binding row is read after each create):

| `succeedsParent` on an explicit non-dashboard successor key | Parent binding after create | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | opt-in rollover |
| **omitted** | `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` | **legacy rollover preserved** (the P1 compatibility contract) |
| `false` | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | opt-out, parallel |
| omitted, minted **dashboard** child | `{"state":"active"}` (intact) | detached by construction — the #106778 path |

A follow-up turn on a genuinely succeeded predecessor fails at the generation fence, as it should — retirement semantics for real successions are unchanged.

- **A reproduces the persisted-state failure #106778 reports, live**: a *successful* detached-dashboard-child create writes a tombstone of the same shape and under the same binding key the issue documents (`entry_key: session-key:main:…`, `value_json {"version":1,"state":"cleared","retired":true,…}`), and the next parent turn fails permanently at the equivalent durable-generation fence in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-binding.ts` while new sessions keep working. (The fence message wording evolved between versions; the issue's build printed "binding generation was retired".)
- **B (this PR) proves both requested paths live**: the parent keeps completing real Codex-backed turns after the detached child is created (producer emits no terminal event — see the built-in detector above), and an explicit `succeedsParent` successor still rolls the parent over, with a real turn completing in the successor session.
- **C (current main)**: the parent binding also survives detached-child creation — #108042's consumer-side guard protects the Codex plugin today. The producer path in `session-create-service.ts` is unchanged between A and C (git history), and tree A demonstrates live what that producer emission does to a pre-guard consumer; any other plugin that treats the parent-terminal hook as terminal remains exposed on main. Because `succeedsParent` does not exist on main, a *genuine* succession also cannot be declared. The two fixes are complementary: #108042 hardens the Codex consumer; this PR fixes the lifecycle contract at the source.


### Persisted-state consequence — proven in-boundary over a real store

The destructive step lives in the Codex extension, and its bundled suite already asserts it over a **real** `createCodexAppServerBindingStore`: `session_end(reason:"new")` retires the generation (`read() → undefined` — the `{"state":"cleared","retired":true}` tombstone #106778 reports), while non-terminal reasons (`shutdown`, `restart`, `compaction`) leave it intact. So the persisted mutation is real and reason-selective — suppressing the parent `session_end` for a parallel child is exactly what keeps the binding alive.

### Gate A/B + validation (real gateway session-create path, deterministic)

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` toggles only the disposition:

```
explicit tui-* successor (succeedsParent)        → parent session_end(reason:"new") + child session_start
minted dashboard child (default)                 → no parent session_end; child session_start
fork                                             → no parent session_end
succeedsParent + {dashboard-keyed|keyless|fork}  → INVALID_REQUEST (no hooks)
```

- **65** focused lifecycle tests (`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` + `server.sessions.create.test.ts`) + **147** TUI tests pass (Node 25.9.0).
- **Static**: `tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` clean.
- **Preservation**: `extensions/codex/` unchanged — a genuine `session_end reason:"new"` still retires the binding.

## Tests

`server.sessions.reset-hooks.test.ts` (explicit `tui-*` successor with `succeedsParent` → parent `session_end` + child `session_start`; detached dashboard child → no parent `session_end`, child `session_start`; reset-in-place + `command:new`/`before_reset` unchanged; **new** — `succeedsParent` + dashboard-keyed child, keyless child, and fork each → `INVALID_REQUEST`), `server.sessions.create.test.ts` (selected-global dashboard child and fork → no parent `session_end`), `tui-command-handlers.test.ts` (`/new` declares `succeedsParent: true`).

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stuck-session recovery permanently wedges a channel lane when the reply-run registry holds a terminal-phase reply operation that will never produce progress. The lane stays stuck until the Gateway restarts.

Two phantom scenarios exist:
1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and unconditionally returns `keep_lane` with `reason=active_reply_work` — the lane is permanently wedged.
2. A ReplyOperation with `phase=running` but zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires.

On current main, `complete()` clears registry state immediately, so "completed" operations are not affected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add two recovery branches before the `active_reply_work` / `keep_lane` gate:

1. **Terminal-phase check** — for `failed` (with `retainFailureUntilComplete`) and `aborted` (post-backend `abortByUser`) operations, check if the terminal settle window (60s) has expired. If so, reclaim the operation via `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` with `forceClear: true`. If still within the settle window, keep the lane.

2. **`fallbackAgeMs` parameter** in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists (`lastProgressAgeMs` is undefined), fall back to the overall session age. Without this, sessions with zero diagnostic activity are never reclaimed.

The fix is scoped to the stuck-session recovery runtime. `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, and `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` are unchanged.

## User Impact

None. This is an internal recovery logic fix. Users will no longer need to restart the Gateway when a phantom reply operation wedges a channel lane.

## Evidence

### Tests (Node 22.22.3)

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Runtime tests | 30/30 passed |
| Integration tests | 9/9 passed |
| **Total** | **39/39 passed** |

### E2E Proof Script

Uses production code paths directly (`createReplyOperation`, `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`, `enqueueCommandInLane`, `diag.warn`) — no test harnesses or mocks.

```
✅ ALL SECTIONS PASSED (5/5)

[1] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (failed):
    → retainFailureUntilComplete + fail → phase="failed"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=failed"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[2] TERMINAL-PHASE RECLAIM (aborted):
    → setPhase("running") + abortByUser → phase="aborted"
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs > 60s)
    → "reclaiming terminal reply operation phase=aborted"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅

[3] HEALTHY ACTIVE REPLY (no false positive):
    → running phase, recent diagnostic activity
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=120s)
    → "active_reply_work" keep_lane
    → status=skipped, healthy reply untouched ✅

[4] SETTLE WINDOW GUARD:
    → terminal operation fresh activity (lastProgressAgeMs ≈ 0)
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=30s, < 60s)
    → "still within settle window"
    → status=skipped, action=keep_lane ✅

[5] NO-PROGRESS PHANTOM:
    → running phase, zero diagnostic events
    → recoverStuckDiagnosticSession(ageMs=720s, fallbackAgeMs fires)
    → "reclaiming stale active reply work"
    → status=aborted, queued message delivered ✅
```

### Captured Diagnostic Output (Terminal-Phase Failed Example)

```
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation:
  sessionId=proof-failed age=120s queueDepth=1 phase=failed

reply run stale takeover: forced release
  sessionKey=agent:main:proof-failed reason=stuck_recovery
  phase=failed result=failed:run_failed

stuck session recovery:
  action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=1

stuck session recovery outcome:
  status=aborted aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=1
  queuedCount=1
```

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` | +24/-15 — terminal-phase branch for failed/aborted + `fallbackAgeMs` param |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | +4/-2 — narrow `it.each` to failed/aborted, settle window test uses failed |
| `src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | +6/-2 — conflict resolution, comment updates |

target.title: fix(ui): bound chat avatar metadata and image fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` issues two `fetch` calls — the avatar metadata lookup and the local avatar image download — **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled gateway leaves avatar resolution pending indefinitely, blocking the chat header update.

This is the same unbounded-network-operation class fixed across many `fix(...)` "bound X" PRs: a request with no `AbortSignal` can hang the caller forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`CHAT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`) around both fetches, matching the Control UI convention used by `agent-select.ts` (`AGENT_SELECT_AVATAR_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`). The timer is cleared in `finally`.

## User Impact

Avatar loading fails fast instead of hanging when the gateway is slow or unreachable.

## Evidence

- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts` on `main`: both `fetch` calls have no `signal`.
- Fix threads `controller.signal` into both requests and clears the timeout.

Co-Authored-By: opencode <noreply@opencode.ai>
## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Chat avatar resolution (`refreshChatAvatar` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.ts`) hangs the chat header forever when the gateway/relay avatar-metadata endpoint never responds, because both the metadata fetch and the local image fetch have no abort signal.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin. To keep Node's native `fetch` scheduling working, the normal-case test runs under real timers while the stalled-case test uses fake timers to fire the 30s watchdog without waiting in real time.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-avatar.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
 - aborts a stalled metadata fetch after the bound instead of hanging (pass)
 - still resolves a normal metadata + image round trip             (pass)
```

Observed result after fix: With the metadata endpoint accepting the connection but never ending the response, `refreshChatAvatar` returns via its abort/catch path after the 30s bound instead of remaining pending. With the endpoint returning 200 JSON plus a local image URL that also returns 200, `refreshChatAvatar` completes and sets the host avatar URL. Ordinary avatar loading is unaffected.

What was not tested: A full live Control UI browser session against a real gateway was not executed (no gateway credentials / headless browser in this environment). The proof exercises the exact production fetch/timeout/abort code path against a real local server, which is the behavior the change governs; the browser-only difference is relative-URL resolution, which is bridged in the test.

target.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ambient transcript watermarks could treat non-decimal message ids such as `0x12` or `1e3` as ordered numbers when multiple messages share the same timestamp. That could advance or suppress the watermark using a numeric interpretation the channel did not actually provide.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watermark comparison now uses numeric ordering only for canonical non-negative decimal integer message ids. Other ids use a stable string boundary in both watermark persistence and Telegram history filtering, so equal-timestamp replay cannot move the stored boundary backward just because a different non-decimal id appears.

## User Impact

Users and operators get more reliable ambient transcript replay boundaries for channels that emit message ids that look numeric but are not canonical decimal integers.

## Evidence

Current head: `2860f40f5dfb4b918393cc4a7949a19dce6a6333`

- GitHub `Real behavior proof` passed on the current head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29612810770/job/87991156445
- Focused regression suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/ambient-transcript-watermark.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.test.ts` passed 31 tests across the session watermark and Telegram history-filter surfaces.
- Whitespace check: `git diff --check` passed.

<details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. The change uses one surrogate-safe helper for the 50-code-unit assistant bash preview, the 40-code-unit generic argument preview, and the shared sidebar truncation path used by persisted `bashExecution` records. It preserves the existing limits and ellipsis behavior while dropping a boundary surrogate half instead of emitting invalid text.

This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

Exported HTML transcripts now show stable compact tool labels when long commands or arguments contain emoji at a truncation boundary. Existing ASCII previews and their length limits remain unchanged.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{

  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",

      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.

With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. The stale event base SHA made base-branch changes look like pull-request changes, consuming macOS runners and adding irrelevant checks.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Current head: `32452922d779597437621cdf63fb02d740b49837`.
- Dependency contract checked in Crabbox source: config files load before environment overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` overrides the configured provider, and an explicit CLI `--provider` remains the final override.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Remote Testbox delegation was unavailable because the installed Crabbox binary is 0.16.0 while the current flow requires 0.22.0 or newer. The proof above is secretless local execution, and GitHub CI remains the remote verification lane.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
